_comment_version_1_17_6: 1.17.5 -> 1.17.6: the last IS_DEMO site in this manifest is gone. The onboarding-complete integration injected `const isDemo = bool.fromEnvironment('IS_DEMO', defaultValue: false)` into the host's onboarding_route_pages.dart and routed a parent/guardian to /partner-dashboard behind it. base_sdk 1.65.0 made that define a no-op, so the const was always false and the branch was unreachable: a demo parent landed on /partner-accept-invite instead of the partner side they were meant to preview. The branch now reads DemoSession.demoActive at the point of the decision, which is also what makes it correct for a demo ACCOUNT - the session flips on minutes after boot, where the build flag never could. Both onboarding_slides entries declare the narrow package:base_sdk/src/services/demo_session.dart import so the composer's @generated-onboarding-imports block carries the symbol into the shell; the imports are a deduped set, so declaring it twice adds one line. No demo fixture, copy or interface changed. Version bumped so version-aware cache reconciliation re-applies the integration in every shell.
_comment_version_1_17_5: 1.17.3 -> 1.17.5: the ten `bool.fromEnvironment('IS_DEMO')` locals in templates/routes/lms_route_pages.dart now read DemoSession.demoActive. These were not a compile failure - an undefined dart-define is simply false - and that was the whole problem: IS_DEMO was deleted from base_sdk in 1.65.0, so every one of the ten resolved to a CONST false and its demo branch was unreachable code. The demo and tour behaviour they gate was silently dead: _partnerProfileDeps and PartnerDashboardRouteView always built the Http/Kv partner sources, so the parent-role preview hit the access gate and rendered empty; _partnerMonthlyRate always asked a backend that is not there, so the partner cost card stayed hidden; LessonReviewRouteView always read the published operator index; supachargeAnnouncementsAllowed always asked the server gate, which fails closed with no backend and hid the Announcements row outright, and AnnouncementsAdminRouteView / HomeworkFulfilmentRouteView behind it always served the Http admin and landed on a retry state; SponsorDashboardRouteView, LeagueRouteView and EntitlementsRouteView each always took their HTTP source, so /sponsor-reports, /league and /my-plan previewed as retry states or zeros. Every one is now resolved at the point of use - inside the ternary or the `if`, on the call or the build that needs it - and NOT held in a local, a field or a final, because a demo account signs in minutes after boot and a sign-out ends the session mid-run. supachargeAnnouncementsAllowed needed more than a token swap: it memoised its one `can_manage_announcements` ask in a single `_announcementsAccess` Future, which would have made the demo/real DECISION sticky for the whole run - the first ask pins one side and a later sign-in keeps reading the other side's settled answer. The cache is now per side (_announcementsAccessDemo / _announcementsAccessLive), so it still asks once per run per side and a session flip lands on the next call. No demo fixture changed, no copy changed and no interface changed. NOT covered here: this file's 33 remaining `AppConstants.isDemo` reads (32 here and one in demo_lesson.dart) are the subject of a separate open PR, and nothing in this package's analyzer or test surface grades templates/ at all - analysis_options.yaml excludes templates/** and no test imports this file - so these ten were migrated by reading, not by a failing check. Version bumped so version-aware cache reconciliation re-extracts the composed lms_route_pages.dart into every shell; 1.17.4 and 1.18.0 are claimed by open PRs, so this takes 1.17.5.
_comment_version_1_17_4: 1.17.3 -> 1.17.4: the host composer templates read DemoSession.demoActive instead of the deleted AppConstants.isDemo - a build fix, no behaviour change for either kind of session, no new seam and no new demo data. base_sdk 1.65.0 deleted AppConstants.isDemo, DemoSession.isDemoOverride and the IS_DEMO dart-define outright, so every read of that member is a hard compile error ("Member not found: 'isDemo'", Target kernel_snapshot_program failed) and the composed supacharge build could not get past the front-end. 1.17.0 took the last such read out of this SDK's lib/ and test/ but deliberately left templates/ alone as shell code; those 33 reads are what was still failing the build - 32 in templates/routes/lms_route_pages.dart and 1 in templates/routes/demo_lesson.dart. Each is now DemoSession.demoActive, read AT THE POINT OF THE DECISION rather than captured, which is what makes this correct rather than merely compiling: demoActive is `AppConstants.isTour || DemoSession.instance.active`, so unlike the old compile-time constant it CHANGES while the app runs - a server-marked demo account signing in flips it on minutes after DI ran, and a sign-out flips it back. Two sites therefore could not be a straight swap. _SupachargeNavState held `bool _subscribed = AppConstants.isDemo`, a field initialiser that pinned the 4th nav slot to whichever side was active when the nav mounted; _subscribed is now the KV access gate's answer alone (false until it lands) and a new `_profileSlot` GETTER returns `DemoSession.demoActive || _subscribed`, so the slot is re-resolved on every build AND again inside onSelect when it is tapped, which can be many frames and one sign-in later - the tap handler read `!_subscribed` directly before, so a straight field swap would have painted Profile and opened the plans page. _SubscribePageState held `final LessonPlans _plans = ... ? ... : ...`, caching the SIDE for the life of the page; it now keeps both sides as fields and picks per read through a getter, because SubscriptionsLessonPlansAdapter caches its last catalog fetch so purchase(planId) resolves the chosen plan without a second round trip and a fresh instance per read would go cold. Everything else is the same expression with the same operands in the same place - the access-status gate, the plan snapshot, the student-grade fallback, the AudioSync clock client, both tutor avatars, the assistant and break-Q&A stand-ins, the chat plan gate, the next-lesson prompt's schedule and skills, the knowledge-bite and skill-review sources, the covered-lesson resolver, the partner-side latch, the linked-student read, the rollover baseline and performance, the Schedule and Library sources and stores, the discovery sample and snippets, and the profile entitlements source. Comments that named `--dart-define=IS_DEMO=true` as the trigger for one of these 33 decisions now say "a demo session"; the demo_lesson seeder's skip log says "no demo session" instead of "not a demo build". NOTHING was migrated beyond those 33 reads: the file's 10 `bool.fromEnvironment('IS_DEMO')` locals compile fine (an undefined define is simply false) and are left exactly as they are, and auth's deliberate AppConstants.isTour gate is untouched. No public API changed, no tr_keys moved and no test was skipped or quarantined - the standalone suite's 41 pre-existing failures (40 suites that cannot load because base_sdk's TrKeys has not had this manifest's tr_keys injected, plus tr_keys_injection_guard_test which reports exactly that) are unchanged, and templates/ is excluded from analysis by analysis_options.yaml, so the composed supacharge build is the gate this fixes. Version bumped so version-aware cache reconciliation re-extracts the composed lms_route_pages.dart and demo_lesson.dart into every shell.
_comment_version_1_17_3: 1.17.2 -> 1.17.3: theme-mode correctness for the holiday, practice and league surfaces and for five widgets those pages own - colours only, no layout, no copy and no new seam. HolidayProgrammePage, PracticePage and LeaguePage each decided their Scaffold fill and ink from mode-resolving AppStyle statics with nothing in their builds that a theme-mode flip reschedules, and all three are auto_route pages: AutoRoutePage.buildPage hands the route the very child instance the route view made, so an ancestor rebuild re-wraps an identical widget and Element.updateChild short-circuits. LeaguePage shows why being a ConsumerWidget is no defence - its ref.watch is on engagementProvider, which fires on league data and never on the mode. Each build now reads `Theme.of(context).brightness` ONCE, outside every inner builder, and hands it down to its helpers (holiday's _buildShelves, practice's _emptyState/_question/_option/_summary), resolving through base_sdk 1.66.7's explicit-brightness seams (surfaceFor / cardFor / cardAltFor / strokeFor / subtleStrokeFor / inkFor / secondaryInkFor / faintFor). Five widgets take a theme dependency of their own because their host pins them: holiday's _Notice and PendingSyncNotice are built `const` (the set-your-grade and packing-shelf notices, and the profile sections' sync notice), and PageDots, McqOverlay, SpeakerBubble and CalendarExportBanner are built from pages that do not rebuild on a flip at all. McqOverlay hands its brightness down to _content, which all three of its shapes (panel, sheet, overlay) build from. No colour value changed in either mode. Everything these pages build non-`const` from their own build is deliberately UNTOUCHED and still reads the statics - league's four cards and standings row, holiday's _LessonCard, practice's option tiles, McqOverlay's _OptionTile - because the fixed parent's rebuild hands each a fresh instance. New theme_mode_student_surfaces_test carries ten widget-level assertions that fail on the previous version and pass here, plus one source guard for CalendarExportBanner, whose LessonCalendarPrefs has no injectable seam for the profile switch it needs before it paints. Version bumped so version-aware cache reconciliation re-resolves the SDK into every shell.
_comment_version_1_17_2: 1.17.1 -> 1.17.2: theme-mode correctness for the three operator surfaces - colours only, no layout, no copy and no new seam. A mutable static is not an inherited widget, so the flip notified nobody, and each of these is an auto_route page: AutoRoutePage.buildPage hands the route the very child instance the route view made, so a Navigator update re-wraps that identical instance and Element.updateChild short-circuits - no ancestor rebuild can reach the page. Each build now reads `Theme.of(context).brightness` ONCE, outside the list builder, hands it down to its _buildList helper, and resolves through base_sdk 1.66.7's explicit-brightness seams (surfaceFor / inkFor / secondaryInkFor). The cards, retry states and BOTH dialogs in these files are deliberately UNTOUCHED: the cards and retry states are built non-`const` from their page's own build, and _ComposeDialog / _PublishDialog are showDialog content, which a Navigator update rebuilds outright - Navigator's didUpdateWidget and didChangeDependencies call Route.changedExternalState, ModalRoute clears its cached page and the showDialog builder runs again, so both dialogs get a fresh instance and the statics resolve against the mode the flip has already set. New theme_mode_admin_surfaces_test proves both halves rather than assuming them: nine assertions that fail on the previous version and pass here, and two that pass on both (the dialogs) which pin the rejection. Version bumped so version-aware cache reconciliation re-resolves the SDK into every shell.
_comment_version_1_17_1: 1.17.0 -> 1.17.1: theme-mode correctness for the billing, downloads and term-report surfaces - colours only, no layout, no copy and no new seam. Each of BillingHistoryPage, EntitlementsPage, StorageManagerPage and TermReportPage decided its Scaffold fill, app-bar ink and secondary ink from mode-resolving AppStyle statics (surfaceDark, textPrimary, textDarkSecondary), and none of their builds read anything a theme-mode flip reschedules. The cards, rows and retry states inside these four pages are deliberately UNTOUCHED and still read the statics: each is constructed non-`const` from its page's own build, so the page's rebuild hands it a fresh instance and the statics resolve against the mode the flip has already set - new theme_mode_billing_storage_report_test asserts exactly that for _RetryState and _LessonRow alongside the four page subjects and the const note, each pumped as a pinned child and flipped without a remount. _comment_version_1_17_0: 1.16.10 -> 1.17.0: the LMS repository (and the tutor catalog over it) are now chosen by the RUNTIME demo session instead of the compile-time IS_DEMO build flag. LmsSdkDependencies.register decided once at launch on AppConstants.isDemo, so a production build ALWAYS registered HttpLmsRepository; when a server-marked demo account signed in afterwards (auth_sdk calls DemoSession.instance.activate() on the backend's is_demo_account marker, minutes after DI ran) every LMS screen kept calling the rlms backend for that session - ServerClock.sync() -> serverTime(), the schedule -> listCourses()/schedule, tutor discovery -> listTutors() - and showed schedule-unavailable or a server error whenever the backend was off. New SessionSwitchingLmsRepository (exported) holds both sides and resolves `DemoSession.demoActive ? demoRepo : httpRepo` INSIDE every one of the interface's methods, so the sign-in lands on the very next call with no re-registration and a sign-out lands the same way in reverse; new SessionSwitchingTutorCatalog (exported) does the same for TutorCatalog, which needs its own switch because BackendTutorCatalog caches its fetched deck and a warm cache would otherwise outlive the session flip. The AppConstants.isDemo branches are GONE from both registrations: DemoSession.demoActive is `isDemo || DemoSession.instance.active`, so a demo BUILD still serves the same DemoLmsRepository / SeededTutorCatalog fixtures it always did, and this SDK's DI no longer names the build flag at all. The existing demo fixtures are reused unchanged - no new demo data. LmsUploadQueue.instance.install() is now unconditional (it was gated on !AppConstants.isDemo): the queue is fed only by HttpLmsRepository's retryQueue, DemoLmsRepository never enqueues, and a drain kick on an empty outbox is a no-op, so this is exactly what every non-demo build already did while anything it does drain is a real pending write that must still reach the backend. Deliberately NO backend-failure fallback was added: a real session's HTTP error propagates untouched so a production problem stays visible instead of reading as seed data. New session_switching_lms_repository_test covers both directions, the per-call re-resolution, the demo-build case and the catalog seam. The last two WIDGET-level `AppConstants.isDemo` reads in this SDK go with it, because the per-call switch makes them redundant for a demo session and dead for everything else: TheBoardPage held `term ?? (AppConstants.isDemo ? BoardTerm.demo(subject: subject) : null)` and SchedulePage passed the identical fallback as the session card's `boardTerm`. DemoLmsRepository.boardCoverage already returns exactly `BoardTerm.demo(subject: subject)`, so the Board's own coverage fetch - which now runs for every session, not just real ones - delivers the representative term to a demo BUILD and a demo SIGN-IN alike through SessionSwitchingLmsRepository; the page keeps honouring an injected term and otherwise fetches. On the schedule side the private _SessionCard's `boardTerm` parameter and its _boardSnippet builder are removed outright rather than left reachable-by-nobody: that page has no coverage read of its own, the build-flag fallback was the snippet's ONLY source, and demo data is never a fallback (decision #47) - keeping the widget alive on fixtures is exactly what was ruled dead. No production build ever rendered it (it required IS_DEMO), no public API changes (_SessionCard is private to schedule_page.dart) and no tr_keys are orphaned (`theBoard` and `bandsCovered` are still read by TheBoardPage); giving the card a real LmsRepository.boardCoverage-backed snippet, which would now work for a demo session as well as a real one, is left as its own change. Neither page imports base_sdk's `app_constants.dart` any more and `AppConstants.isDemo` is now read NOWHERE in lms/dart/lib or lms/dart/test - only in doc comments that explain what replaced it. The host composer templates under `templates/` keep their own build-flag branches: that is shell code, outside this SDK's runtime, and it is deliberately untouched. Version bumped so version-aware cache reconciliation re-resolves the SDK into every shell.
_comment_version_1_16_10: 1.16.9 -> 1.16.10: curriculum badge honesty only, no layout and no new seam. The schedule header and the Library showed the student's STORED curriculum as a badge over lessons that are always served from the CAPS index - the published lesson indexes carry CAPS rows only, the index builders read the CAPS curriculum root and lms_course has no curriculum dimension - so a student who picked an IEB school in onboarding read an "IEB" badge over CAPS content. The badge asserts "these lessons are <X>", which was not true for any value but CAPS. New kServedCurricula ({kSupachargeCurriculum}) names the curricula whose lessons actually reach a student, and new resolveContentCurriculumLabel() returns the stored curriculum only when it is in that set, else null; both badge hosts (ScheduleRouteView, LibraryRouteView) resolve through it and hold String? instead of String. No SDK change was needed: SchedulePage.curriculum and LibraryPage.curriculum are already String? and both already guard `if (widget.curriculum != null)`, so null simply paints no badge. resolveStudentCurriculum() is deliberately unchanged - the stored value keeps flowing to the school-capture flow, whose "CAPS - change?" chip reports which school pool matched during data capture and is not a content claim. Adding a curriculum to kServedCurricula once its content ships restores its badge on its own. Version bumped so version-aware cache reconciliation re-extracts the composed lms_route_pages.dart into every shell.

boot_hooks._comment: Registers this SDK's bundled Afrikaans map for its manifest tr_keys into base_sdk's BundledTranslations registry at boot. Backend-served translation rows still win; the map is only the offline/unseeded fallback consulted before the humanized-key fallback. Requires a base_sdk with bundled_translations.dart.

di_hooks._comment: Registers every lms profile section (student rows, partner billing/students cards, shared theme-toggle/nav-clearance) with base_sdk's ProfileSectionRegistry, plus the registry's onLogout callback - the sections base_sdk's GenericProfilePage renders on /profile and /partner-profile. Runs directly after the generated sdk-di block so GetIt already holds LmsRepository. Declared top-level, NOT in an app_type flavor block, because this SDK's Dart manifest has no flavor blocks: Supacharge is one binary serving both personas, and student-vs-partner is a runtime role - the persona split lives in the sections' visibility gates, driven by which profile route is on screen (see registerSupachargeProfileSections in the installed lms_route_pages.dart). Requires base_sdk >= 1.27.0 (the profile host with identity-header slots: the student grade badge and stat row register into the header card's badge/stats slots). Since 1.12.0 this hook also configures wallet_sdk's WalletCardSection static seam (student-persona gate + 'R' symbol) for the 'wallet.card' section wallet_sdk registers via its own di_hook - the installed lms_route_pages.dart therefore imports wallet_sdk, so compositions including lms_sdk need wallet_sdk >= 1.2.0 (the section + config seam; supacharge, this SDK's only consumer, already composes wallet_sdk).

_comment_platform_permissions: Dormant until the calendar plugin ships: declares the device-calendar access the planned timetable sync will request. Declared permissions are inert until requested at runtime, so hosts composing lms_sdk today gain the manifest/plist entries without any behavior change - when the plugin lands, no host needs a platform-file edit.

ios.NSCalendarsUsageDescription: Your device calendar is used to sync class timetables and assignment due dates you choose to add.

_comment_constants_identity: appTitle/appMotto re-point base_sdk's neutral JUVO app identity at Supacharge's own name and motto (SupachargeConstants). Read by AppHelpers.getAppName's fallback and by comms_sdk's MockSettingsRepository, which seeds the demo 'title' setting and 'motto' translation from them — so demo builds (and the guided tour) show Supacharge branding on the onboarding welcome card instead of the kernel's shared defaults.
_comment_session_policy: Declared by lms_sdk as the app's home SDK (auth_sdk manifest's _comment_session_policy documents the seam: sdk_installer_base.py's update_session_policy() turns this into the DeclaredSessionPolicy assignment in the installed auth_session_policy.dart shell). One fallback entry only: every authenticated account — any role, and role-less/offline sessions too — is ADMITTED with its session kept and lands on /schedule, the same route replaceMainRoute above already resolves the production goHome landing to. So production sign-ins land bit-for-bit where they always did; what changes is demo (--dart-define=IS_DEMO=true), whose undeclared-policy default was the legacy isDemo -> replaceUiTypeRoute branch: demo logins used to land on the marketplace /ui-type chooser, which is not part of this app, and now land on the app's own home. With '*' declared nothing is ever rejected, so no rejection_message_tr_key/rejection_route are declared. Partner-role accounts also land on /schedule (as they did via goHome before); the partner surfaces stay reachable exactly as today — via onboarding's parent branch and the partner routes.
_comment_brand_hook: Injects the app's brand palette into the shared AppStyle tokens before the first frame (the kernel ships neutral defaults only). lms_sdk declares it as supacharge's home SDK; applyAppBrandColors itself is defined in lib/presentation/theme/theme.dart, which base_sdk's installs deliver (templates/theme -> lib/presentation/theme) — the host customizes that installed copy with its palette. At most one SDK in an app may declare brand_hook; the installer errors on conflict.
_comment_splash_assets: Home SDKs ship the splash/login background images (base_sdk's splash_page and auth_sdk's login_page reference assets/images/splash*.png). Each home SDK provides its own copies so every composed app can brand them independently; the app_assets entries below get them into the host pubspec's sdk-app-assets block so they are actually bundled. If the host (or base_sdk) already has identical files on disk, the file copy is skipped (already-present guard) and only the pubspec declaration matters.
_onboarding_comment: onboarding_slides inject lms's student steps into onboarding_sdk's shell template (see sdk_installer_base.py's update_onboarding_slides()). School BEFORE grade (owner's ordering): picking the school derives and stores the curriculum, so by the time the grade step shows, the flow already knows which level structure applies. Both are student-only — a parent setting the account up for their child is not the one with a school/grade. The integrations entry extends the shell's completion routing: in demo builds a parent/guardian lands straight on the partner dashboard so the reporting experience is previewable without a real partner account. It also carries the TEMPORARY admin branch paired with onboarding_sdk's kShowAdminOnboardingChoice flag: the admin choice routes straight to /profile, where every operator row stays behind its own server gate — delete that branch together with the flag.

onboarding_slides.body:
OnboardingSlide(
  data: const {'id': 'lms.school_capture'},
  roles: const {OnboardingRole.student},
  content: Builder(
    builder: (context) => SchoolSlide(
      capture: LmsSchoolCaptureAdapter(),
      suggester: supachargeSchoolSuggester,
      defaultCurriculum: kSupachargeCurriculum,
      onContinue: () => OnboardingSlideScope.of(context).next(),
    ),
  ),
)

_registration_steps_comment: registration_steps inject the SAME school + grade capture into auth_sdk's post-register pipeline (see sdk_installer_base.py's update_registration_steps() and auth_sdk's templates/routes/registration_step_pages.dart shell): a student who decides NOT to skip register and goes straight to it never sees onboarding, so without this the app had no way to take school and grade from them. Same widgets (SchoolSlide/GradeSlide), same host adapters (LmsSchoolCaptureAdapter -> LmsRepository.setSchool(), LmsGradeCaptureAdapter -> setGrade(), both offline-first via the shared KV), same school-before-grade ordering and for the same reason. skippable stays default-true inside the RegistrationStep(...) bodies — a failed or skipped capture must never trap a fresh account; the profile offers both fields again later. No roles here: registration has no role step, and the direct-register path is the student's.

registration_steps.body:
RegistrationStep(
  data: const {'id': 'lms.school_capture'},
  content: Builder(
    builder: (context) => SchoolSlide(
      capture: LmsSchoolCaptureAdapter(),
      suggester: supachargeSchoolSuggester,
      defaultCurriculum: kSupachargeCurriculum,
      onContinue: () => RegistrationStepScope.of(context).next(),
    ),
  ),
)
